title: Farage elected MP for Clacton
detail: Nigel Farage wins Clacton for Reform UK with 46.2% of the vote and a majority of 8,405 — a 45.1-point swing from the Conservatives, the largest at any UK general election.

title: Standards investigation opened
detail: The Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards opens an investigation into a £5 million personal gift to Farage from cryptocurrency investor Christopher Harborne, which was not declared to parliamentary authorities. Farage says the gift was for his personal security and denies breaking any rules.

title: Further revelations
detail: A Sunday Times investigation reports that Farage's work was financially supported by his adviser George Cottrell, a convicted criminal, without the required declarations. The Liberal Democrats call for the standards inquiry to be expanded. Farage describes the investigations as an "establishment hit job".

title: Farage resigns, forcing a by-election
detail: Rather than await the outcome of the standards process — which could have led to suspension and a recall petition — Farage announces his resignation as MP at a press conference, triggering a by-election in which he intends to stand. "I have done no wrongdoing and followed the rules," he says.

title: Resignation takes effect
detail: Chancellor Rachel Reeves appoints Farage Steward and Bailiff of the Manor of Northstead — the ceremonial office used to vacate a Commons seat, as MPs cannot simply resign. Clacton is formally without an MP from this point until the by-election.

title: Major parties decline to stand
detail: Labour, the Conservatives, the Liberal Democrats, the Greens and Rupert Lowe's Restore Britain all say they will not contest the by-election, variously describing it as a stunt, a "fake by-election" and a media circus. The Conservatives indicate they would fight any subsequent by-election in the seat.

title: Writ moved — polling day set for 13 August
detail: The House of Commons moves the writ, formally starting the by-election and fixing the timetable for nominations, absent-vote deadlines and polling day. Reform UK offers to meet the estimated £200,000 cost of running the contest.

title: A crowded field forms — and some drop out
detail: With the main opposition parties standing aside, dozens of smaller-party and independent candidates come forward, among them the satirical Count Binface, Reclaim's Laurence Fox, the Official Monster Raving Loony Party and Rejoin EU. Several who announced early do not go on to file nomination papers, including Piers Corbyn, Protect the Wild's Rob Pownall and independents Ollie Granger and Luke Worley, who withdrew saying voters wanted a straight two-horse race.

title: Nominations close — a record 34 candidates
detail: Tendring District Council publishes the Statement of Persons Nominated: 34 candidates, the most at any UK parliamentary by-election, beating the 26 who stood at Haltemprice and Howden in 2008. Nineteen are independents and three are Monster Raving Loonies. This is the definitive ballot paper.

title: Deadline to register to vote
detail: Midnight on 28 July is the last moment to get on the electoral register in time to vote in this by-election. Applications for a postal vote close at 5pm the following day, 29 July.

title: Proxy vote and voter ID deadlines
detail: 5pm on 5 August is the deadline both to apply for a proxy vote and to apply for a free Voter Authority Certificate for anyone without an accepted form of photo ID.

title: Polling day
detail: Voting takes place at 51 polling stations across the constituency, open 7am to 10pm. Almost 80,000 electors are eligible. Photo ID is required to vote in person. The count follows immediately, with the result expected in the early hours of 14 August.
